## Academic papers

**Welfare conditionality in Latin America's conditional cash transfers: Models and trends**
Antía, F., Rossel, C., & Karsaclian, S. (2024). *International Journal of Social Welfare*. [doi.org/10.1111/ijsw.12677](https://doi.org/10.1111/ijsw.12677)

> Shows that conditionalities vary across Latin America's CCTs and across time within programs. Drawing on existing conceptualizations of welfare conditionality and the CONDLA dataset, it analyzes the evolution and variation in the design of conditionality in the region.

**Welfare conditionality in OECD countries and in Latin America: A comparative perspective**
Antía, F., Immervoll, H., Knotz, C. M., & Rossel, C. (forthcoming). *Global Social Policy*.

> Analyzes the core elements of benefit conditionality rules in the OECD and in Latin America through a common measurement framework, and their implications for studying conditional social policy from a global perspective.

**The Politics of Conditionality in Latin America's Cash Transfer Reforms**
Antía, F. & Rossel, C.

> Analyzes the heterogeneity in the design of conditionalities across Latin America's conditional cash transfer programs and the political dynamics behind the different models.

**The politics of sanctioning the poor through welfare conditionality: Revealing causal mechanisms in Uruguay**
Antía, F. & Rossel, C.

> Using process tracing on the Uruguayan case, shows how electoral competition and public opinion led a left-wing government to tighten the enforcement of conditionalities so as not to alienate its non-beneficiary electoral base.

## Policy brief

**What are conditionalities in social policy? Towards an integrative concept**
Antía, F. & Rossel, C. — [download PDF](publicaciones/policy-brief-condicionalidades.pdf) (in Spanish)

> Reviews advances in the literature on conceptualizing conditionalities and develops a new concept, operationalized for Latin America's Conditional Cash Transfer programs, that makes it possible to study them across policy fields and regions.
